title: Independent Living Residency Agreement — Article on the Annual Review of the Monthly Service Fee
content:
## Article 6 — Annual review

6.1 The monthly service fee of an Independent Living Residency Agreement is reviewed once a year, and an increase normally takes effect on the first day of the normal annual effective month of the apartment type.

6.2 Written notice of each increase is mailed to the resident and recorded with its date and the proposed fee.

6.3 *Retired clause.* The clause under which the fee recorded when the increase takes effect was the proposed fee from that notice is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the recorded fee.

6.4 An increase may be recorded, and may take effect, only on or after the date that is the minimum written notice period of the apartment type after written notice of the increase is mailed to the resident. Notice days are counted in calendar days from the day after the notice is mailed, so the increase may take effect on the date equal to the mailing date plus the notice period in calendar days or any later date.

6.5 No increase may take effect within the new-resident rate guarantee, in calendar months after the move-in date; a resident whose guarantee ends after the normal effective date receives that year's increase on the first day of the calendar month following the end of the guarantee. The guarantee ends on the same day number that many calendar months after the move-in date, falling back to the last day of that month when the day number does not exist.

6.6 The residency must be in active or notice given status for an increase notice or an increase to be recorded.

6.7 *Retired clause.* The clause under which the new fee could not exceed the fee in effect immediately before by more than the contractual ceiling percentage, rounded to the cent half up, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the increase ceiling. The remainder of the sentence stays in force: a residency receives at most one increase in any 12-month period.

6.8 When an increase is recorded after fees for the effective month were already billed at the old fee, the difference for the days from the effective date is charged as a prorated rate change charge; when a fee is reduced on correction, the difference is returned as a rate change proration credit referencing the original charge.

6.9 The base fees published for new agreements do not change the fee of an existing residency except through this article.

## The two clocks at their boundaries (hypothetical dates; 60-day notice, 12-month guarantee)

**Notice clock** — anchored on the mailing date recorded on the residency:

| Increase effective date | Allowed? |
|---|---|
| Mailing date plus 59 calendar days | No |
| Mailing date plus 60 calendar days | Yes |
| Any later date | Yes |

A notice mailed on October 15 allows an increase on December 14 or later; a notice mailed on November 2 allows an increase on January 1 or later.

**Guarantee clock** — anchored on the move-in date recorded on the residency:

| Move-in date | Guarantee ends | Earliest effective date of that year's increase when the normal date is January 1 |
|---|---|---|
| March 15 of one year | March 15 of the next year | April 1 of the next year |
| February 29 of a leap year | February 28 of the next year (fallback to the last day of the month) | March 1 of the next year |
| November 30 of one year | November 30 of the next year | That year's January 1 increase falls inside the guarantee; it is received on December 1 of the next year |

An increase can take effect only after the day on which the guarantee ends, never on that day or earlier.

## Status table

| Residency status | Increase notice or increase may be recorded? |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Notice given | Yes |
| Reserved, vacated, closed, cancelled | No |

superseded_clauses: the fee recorded when the increase takes effect is the proposed fee from that notice
